extracted.intended_audience: American poets, critics, and readers; aspiring writers of national/democratic poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical criteria for composing poetry suited to the United States and its democratic spirit: emphasizes originality, embodiment of national identity, integration of modern science and spirituality, and stylistic choices (form, obscurity, emotional force).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original, native poetry as national proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The topmost proof of a race is its own born poetry; 'the stamp of entire and finished greatness to any nation... must be sternly withheld till it has put what it stands for in the blossom of original, first-class poems. No imitations will do.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems must be autochthonic—born expressers of the nation's spirit rather than faithful imitations of foreign tones (e.g., English diction). The critic's complaint that American verse 'seems an exotic' lacking 'principle of reproduction' is an anti-pattern to avoid: poets should develop a distinctly American idiom and internal evidence of place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as an expression of democracy (emotion and physique)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Leaves of Grass entire is not to be construed as an intellectual or scholastic effort... but more as a radical utterance out of the Emotions and the Physique—in its very nature regardless of the old conventions, and, under the great laws, following only its own impulses.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize visceral, emotional, bodily sources—radical utterance tied to democratic life—over purely scholastic or decorous forms. Poetry should arise from lived, ordinary democratic experience rather than elite abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate modern science — the kosmic spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The real poems of the present... must vocalize the vastness and splendor and reality with which scientism has invested man and the universe... this tremendous innovation, the kosmic spirit, which must henceforth... be the background and underlying impetus, more or less visible, of all first-class songs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and interiorly adopt scientific knowledge; use it to expand poetic scope and imagery (vastness, new orbits, subtle systems). Science should revivify themes and provide new metaphysical background without denying past themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include spiritual/immortality dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It is no less than this idea of immortality, above all other ideas, that is to enter into, and vivify, and give crowning religious stamp, to democracy in the New World.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should engage the eternal, the soul, and religious/spiritual concerns (not merely materialist scientism). Scientism's office is to free theology from fables and enable ampler, diviner songs—prophet and bard to mediate the divine to democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form must grow from purport and facts (form follows content)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Thus my form has strictly grown from my purports and facts, and is the analogy of them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose or invent poetic forms that suit the subject matter and purpose; expect dual forms (prose and poetic) where appropriate. Avoid imposing artificial forms that contradict the work's purport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow obscurity and an aerial, indefinite poetic style
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Human thought, poetry or melody, must leave dim escapes and outlets—must possess a certain fluid, aerial character, akin to space itself, obscure to those of little or no imagination,—but indispensable to the highest purposes. Poetic style, when address'd to the soul, is less definite form... and becomes vista, music, half-tints.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fear charges of obscurity; poetic address to the soul can be purposely indefinite, suggestive, and musical rather than tightly defined. Anti-pattern: over-definiteness that kills the 'fluid' or 'aerial' quality necessary to reach imaginative readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrate ordinary identity — the poem of average Identity
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘A man is not greatest as victor in war... To the highest democratic view, man is most acceptable in living well the practical life and lot which happens to him as ordinary farmer, sea-farer, mechanic... To sing the Song of that law of average Identity, and of Yourself, consistently with the divine law of the universal, is a main intention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on ordinary people, everyday occupations and civic roles as central poetic subjects; elevate practical life and conscience as sources of dignity and the poem's moral center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superficial lyricism and mere ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Poetry, so largely hitherto and even at present wedded to children's tales, and to mere amorousness, upholstery and superficial rhyme, will have to accept... the kosmic spirit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of poems that are only pretty sound, light amorous verse, or decorative technical show. Aim for substantive scope (scientific, spiritual, civic) rather than ornament alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create national types and physiognomy
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘With the poems of a first-class land are twined... its types of personal character, of individuality, peculiar, native, its own physiognomy, man's and woman's, its own shapes, forms, and manners.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use poetry to forge and reveal distinctive national personae and character types—native individuals whose manners and identities help define the nation's culture and imaginative life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance foreign influences with native development
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘If we are not to hospitably receive and complete the inaugurations of the old civilizations... what on earth are we for? ... Allowing all the evil that it did, we get... a balance of good out of its reminiscence almost beyond price.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept useful foreign (e.g., English, European) influences but transform and enlarge them on a broader scale; do not slavishly imitate—aim to fuse and produce distinctively American expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster comradeship and social welding
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It is by a fervent, accepted development of comradeship, the beautiful and sane affection of man for man... that the United States of the future... are to be most effectually welded together.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry can serve a political/social mission: cultivate bonds of comradeship and mutual affection across regional and social divides to strengthen national unity. Anti-pattern: poetry that isolates or only panders to sectional sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to arouse and initiate rather than to define or finish
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The poetry of the future aims at the free expression of emotion... and to arouse and initiate, more than to define or finish.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer poems that stimulate feeling, action, and new perspectives over those that attempt exhaustive explanation or closure. Emphasize initiation, stirring, and opening rather than neat conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve the civic/national pedagogical function
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘I bequeath poems and essays as nutriment and influences to help truly assimilate and harden, and especially to furnish something toward what the States most need of all... to show them, or begin to show them, themselves distinctively, and what they are for.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat literature as nourishment for the nation's self-understanding and moral development. Poems should help form national consciousness and provide the cultural materials the republic lacks.
